evals.name: sprint14-asana-batch-plan
evals.prompt: The Asana connection will be set up tomorrow, so nothing can be written today. Using backlog.md and project-export.json, plan Sprint 14 for the Payments Platform project and write create-plan.md: the exact batch of Asana writes you will make once it is connected, for my approval. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, state it, and finish the work.
evals.expected_output: The skill fixes capacity defaults (10 points per person, 1 point = 1 day), caps leaf tasks at 5 points, puts points only on leaves, maps epics to sections or parent tasks since sections cannot nest, checks for a Story Points custom field, and asks for batch approval. Without it, plans tend to commit the whole backlog, keep 8- and 13-point items whole, and assume a story-points field exists.
expectations: create-plan.md exists
Addresses the 13-point PAY-131 settlement report

Capacity is computed and respected: Uses 10 points per person and adjusts for Lena's 3 PTO days (27 points) or states the 30-point assumption; committed total fits; shows a running used/capacity tally and the 80% warning

Hierarchy and sizing follow the skill: Items over 5 points (PAY-118, PAY-130, PAY-131) are split into leaf tasks of 5 or fewer or deferred; only leaves carry points; epics map to parent tasks or sections without nesting sections

Notices the missing Story Points field: Points out that project-export.json has no Story Points custom field, says points will be tracked locally (or asks the user to add the field), and does not invent a field GID

Plan matches priorities and is executable: Refunds and the PAY-130 ledger export (finance deadline) are in, settlement report deferred; each write names the Sprint 14 section GID, assignee GID from members, a due date within 2026-11-09..20, and the PAY ticket ID in the notes
Honest about the missing connection: Presents the batch for approval and claims nothing was created; no invented task GIDs

evals.name: sprint22-asana-rollover-plan
evals.prompt: Write rollover-plan.md for moving the incomplete tasks from the 'Sprint 22' section to 'Sprint 23' in our Payments Platform Asana project, using sprint-22-open.json. I will run it myself with the Asana MCP tools later. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, state it, and finish the work.
evals.expected_output: The skill's rollover procedure recreates tasks because the MCP has no move-between-sections call, warns about exactly what is lost, needs explicit confirmation and a tag GID from the user, and orders per-task steps so the original is always closed once the copy exists. Without it, a plan usually says 'move the tasks' and loses subtasks and comments silently.
expectations: rollover-plan.md exists
Requires confirmation before executing

Specific data-loss warning and confirmation gate: Warns that recreated tasks lose history, comments, attachments, subtasks, followers, tags and other custom fields, names what that means for these tasks (e.g. PAY-219: 3 subtasks, 11 comments, 4 attachments), and requires explicit confirmation

Per-task step order and failure handling: Create copy, tag original, comment with link, mark original completed; skip the rest if the create fails; always close the original once the copy exists even if tag/comment failed; report both GIDs if closing fails; continue with the next task
Handles the project's actual state: Creates the missing Sprint 23 section first, asks the user for the 'Rolled Over' tag GID (or skips tagging), copies Story Points via the existing custom field
Dates and capacity carried correctly: Due dates shifted 14 days (PAY-212 to 2026-12-02, PAY-219 to 2026-12-04, PAY-215 left blank) and Sprint 23 capacity recalculated with 10 carried points
No assumed capabilities: Does not rely on a move-section call without noting the MCP may not expose it

evals.name: solo-backlog-generic-plan
evals.prompt: Plan my next sprint from backlog.md. I'm a solo developer. Write sprint-plan.md with an estimate for every backlog item, what goes into the sprint and what doesn't, and why. Use your usual defaults for capacity and sprint length. This runs unattended: do not ask questions; state assumptions at the top of the file.
evals.expected_output: Round-2 changed the tracker-neutral rules: split an item over 5 points only if it goes into the sprint, keep deferred items whole, stop around 80 to 90% with stretch items, and mark the 80% point in a written tally. The two Asana evals do not exercise the no-tracker path.
expectations: sprint-plan.md exists
Defaults stated and used: states 10-point capacity, 2-week sprint and 1 point = 1 work day as assumptions and plans to them
Running capacity tally: shows 'Sprint: X/Y pts (Z remaining)' after each item added, marks where usage first reaches 80%, and the committed total is at or under 10

Sizes on the 1/2/3/5/8 scale with sensible anchors: runbook and SDK bump 1, Retry-After 1-2, render.ts tests 2, flaky test or duplicate-push investigation 3, digest feature 5, three-service integration 8

Oversized item handled: item 5 (billing/identity/audit integration) is sized 8 and not scheduled whole; if any part goes in, it is split into proposed leaf tasks of 5 or fewer, otherwise it is deferred whole
Inclusion choices are justified (customer-facing duplicate pushes and CI flakiness prioritized, or a stated rationale) and every deferred item is listed
Leaves slack and names stretch work: does not pack the sprint to exactly 100% without saying why, and lists the next items to pull in if time allows
